legal_form: Charitable company limited by guarantee (registered charity 1154716; registered company 08303764, England & Wales)
site_place: Tunbridge Wells, Kent (borough of Tunbridge Wells and south Tonbridge; area of almost 300 km2)
site_venue: Warehouse / operations centre at Unit 5, Kingstanding Way, North Farm Industrial Estate, Tunbridge Wells, Kent TN2 3UP (occupied since 2021)
site_activity: Volunteers receive and sort food donations and make up emergency food parcels for home delivery, Monday to Friday, every week of the year
last_delivery_what: Home-delivered emergency food parcels (each parcel provides three meals a day for three days) — 15,868 deliveries totalling 142,812 meals to people in food crisis, 46% of recipients children
local_trigger: Rising local food and fuel poverty driven by the cost-of-living crisis; in 2024-25 the leading referral reason was changes to clients' benefits (about 2 in 5 clients), with a rise in Universal Credit cases and increased demand for fuel vouchers

programmes.name: Emergency food parcels
programmes.what: Food parcels providing three nutritious meals a day for three days (staples, tins, fresh produce, toiletries, household items; baby food, nappies, sanitary and pet food when needed), delivered direct to clients' homes by volunteer drivers; typically one parcel per week for four weeks or fewer

programmes.name: Self-referral programme
programmes.what: A self-referral route (introduced after a 2024 trial) letting people apply directly; staff ask screening questions and verify address and identity before approving

programmes.name: Energy/fuel voucher assistance
programmes.what: Vouchers to help clients pay energy bills — £104,016 provided in 2024-25 (mostly from reserves); being wound down once remaining vouchers are distributed, returning focus to core emergency food aid

programmes.name: More than food (signposting)
programmes.what: Operations staff speak with each client/referrer and signpost or refer to specialist agencies for issues such as debt and housing

_certifications_note: APPLICANT-SUPPLIED CERTIFICATIONS (not from public materials): the four boolean administrative self-certifications below are what a real applicant attests on the intake form and are not published anywhere. They are set true here because all four are established registered charities delivering services to vulnerable people, for whom a safeguarding policy, public liability insurance, own-name banking and a conflict-free application are universal and, for safeguarding, legally expected. No specific unknowable detail (e.g. a named Designated Safeguarding Lead) is invented — those stay blank.
